cards.explanation: The answer is encourages. Josiah appoints the priests to their duties and encourages them in the service of the house of the LORD. He doesn't just hand over the job list, he adds a little push of confidence with it. Those are the bosses people remember, friends, because a schedule with a kind word on top goes down a lot easier.

The answer is False. Josiah tells the Levites to put the holy ark in the temple built by Solomon, David's son and a king of Israel. Then he says, “It is not to be carried around on your shoulders.” I bet some Levite shoulders were relieved to hear it.

The answer is their fellow countrymen. Josiah tells the Levites to make preparations for their fellow countrymen. The Levites aren't only getting ready for themselves, friends. Josiah also tells them, "Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel." (2 Chronicles 35:3)

The answer is True. Josiah tells the Levites to prepare so they can carry out “…the word of the LORD given by Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader, and Josiah points them to what he gave. So this whole service rests on something already given, not on a new idea from the king.

The answer is his own flocks and herds. The verse says Josiah contributed the lambs, goats and bulls from his own flocks and herds. That's thirty-three thousand animals coming out of the king's own pocket. When the boss pays for the party himself, friends, you know he means it.

The answer is willingly. The verse says Josiah's officials also contributed willingly to the people, priests and Levites. Nobody had to drag them to the giving table. Willingly is the word the text uses, bakers, and it's the right one.
The answer is False. The verse says the priests splattered the blood handed to them, and the Levites skinned the animals. So it's blood for the priests and skinning for the Levites.

The answer is roasted on the fire. The verse says they roasted the Passover animals on the fire according to the regulation. The other holy offerings were boiled in pots, kettles and bowls. So the Passover animals are the ones that got the fire, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says they boiled the other holy offerings in pots, kettles and bowls and quickly brought them to all the people. Notice the word quickly, bakers. It's right there in verse 13.

The answer is the Levites. The priests were offering burnt offerings and fat until nightfall, so the Levites made preparations for themselves and for the priests. The Levites handled the prep so the priests could keep working. Until nightfall! I get worn out after one double batch, so I respect that.

The answer is King David's. The singers, the descendants of Asaph, were at their stations according to the command of David, king of Israel. The verse also names Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer. Josiah is following a plan that was set up long before him, friends.

The answer is seven days. The verse says the Israelites who were present observed the Passover at that time, as well as the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days. That's a whole week of celebrating. It's a lot longer than one afternoon, bakers.

The answer is Samuel. The verse says, “No such Passover had been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet.” It also says none of the kings of Israel ever observed a Passover like the one Josiah observed. That's a long stretch of time with nothing like it, friends.
